abstracts.value: As superconducting quantum processors scale to large qubit counts, unwanted microwave drive crosstalk becomes an important source of coherent errors. Here, we investigate the role of parasitic coupling paths in the suppression of drive crosstalk in a processor with two fixed-frequency transmon qubits and a tunable coupler. To account for the many different coupling paths, we develop a detailed circuit model to capture the dependence of crosstalk on the coupler frequency. We experimentally demonstrate suppression of crosstalk, finding that the suppression does not originate solely from cancellation of the effective qubit-qubit coupling, but also is a result of interference between other coupling paths. Building on these insights, we show that drive crosstalk can be suppressed with the right choice of parasitic capacitances, which otherwise often are treated as unwanted design imperfections. Our results provide practical guidance for low-crosstalk device design of superconducting quantum processors and point toward a broader strategy in which parasitic coupling paths are engineered rather than simply minimized.

titles.title: Suppressing microwave crosstalk in superconducting quantum processors by designing parasitic drive capacitances

abstracts.value: Live-cell imaging of cellular and tissue samples relies predominantly on optical modalities, such as fluorescence, confocal, and multiphoton microscopy, in which cellular information is encoded in emitted photons. Photons scatter and attenuate in biological samples, restricting depth resolution, while the excitation light required to produce them induces photodamage that perturbs the very biology under observation. Magnetic fields, by contrast, traverse biological samples without attenuation at cellular length scales, but the imaging modality that extracts the encoded information, magnetic resonance imaging, cannot resolve individual cells. Here we present Quantum Cell Monitoring (QCM), a widefield nitrogen-vacancy magnetometry platform that encodes single-cell information in stray magnetic fields rather than emitted photons and reads it out at subcellular resolution. Integrated with a specialized live-cell incubator, QCM tracks magnetically labeled living cancer for up to 72 h through their individual magnetic field signatures. It captures single-cell mitosis and morphological remodeling, as well as cell cluster formation, splitting, and migration even within dense regions where brightfield contrast collapses. By shifting the carrier of single-cell information from propagating optical photons to static magnetic stray fields, QCM decouples cell from cellular optical accessibility and auto-fluorescence, enabling sustained live-cell observation in regimes inaccessible to optical microscopy.

titles.title: Multi-day single-cell magnetic imaging of living cancer cells using Quantum Cell Monitoring

abstracts.value: The beta decay of neutron-rich nuclei probes the microscopic nature of weak interactions in the nuclear medium under extreme conditions. Such weak decays drive the synthesis of heavy elements in astrophysical environments, but remain poorly understood. Far from stability, experimental data are scarce, placing strong demands on ab initio nuclear theory. Two-body weak currents have been proposed as the dominant mechanism responsible for the universal quenching of theoretically predicted Gamow-Teller decay strength. However, direct experimental validation in neutron-rich nuclei has been lacking. Here we measure the beta decay of 54K, a nucleus at the experimental frontier of radioactive ion-beam facilities. In this work, the doubly magic nature of the daughter nucleus 54Ca results in a remarkably simple decay pattern, dominated by a single transition to a neutron-unbound state at 6.2 MeV with a comparative partial half-life logft=4.4(1) or Gamow-Teller decay strength B(GT)=0.26 (+0.08) (-0.04). Our measurement is reproduced by new state-of-the-art calculations of the decay, providing direct evidence for the essential role of two-body currents in nuclear beta decay for systems with a significant neutron excess. We establish a key benchmark for theoretical predictions of weak processes in exotic nuclei.

titles.title: Beta decay of potassium-54 reveals the role of two-body currents in neutron-rich nuclei

abstracts.value: Radio detection of very inclined extensive air showers (EAS) offers a promising way to study ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) and neutrinos above $10^{17}$ eV. We present a method to reconstruct the arrival direction and energy of EAS with zenith angles above $60^\circ$, applicable in principle to upward-going neutrino-induced showers. The approach combines a point-source-like description of the radio wavefront with the Angular Distribution Function (ADF), a phenomenological model describing the angular pattern of electric field amplitudes in the 50-200 MHz band. On realistic cosmic-ray simulations, we achieve better than $0.07^\circ$ resolution on arrival direction and ~15% on primary energy. Applied directly to voltage traces, this method allows efficient cosmic-ray selection with accurate direction reconstruction and first-order energy estimation. We illustrate the method on the first cosmic-ray candidates detected by the GRANDProto300 prototype of GRAND, validating its detection principle and paving the way for high-precision neutrino searches.

titles.title: Reconstruction of very inclined air showers with radio data and application to the first GRANDProto300 cosmic-ray candidates

abstracts.value: While the body of experimental nuclear data continues to grow at a rapid pace, significant gaps persist. The lack of evaluated experimental data is far more pronounced in charged-particle reactions which are essential to a large portion of the isotope production community for vital medical, industrial, and national security interests. In the absence of experimental and evaluated data, isotope production relies on theoretical models that may result in low yield and isotopic impurities. This work investigates model and parameter adjustments in TALYS 2.0 to establish uncertainty bands on proton-induced cross sections, highlight influential parameters in calculations, and constrain adjustments within physically defensible bounds. The EXFOR dataset for proton-induced reactions on natural copper, comprised of 24 independent cross sections, was used for iterative Bayesian model updating. Upon convergence, parameters and their uncertainties were compared against 23 cumulative cross sections from EXFOR, highlighting the limitations of generalization. Various machine learning models were leveraged to predict TALYS performance, with a small neural network showing useful ranking capabilities across several generations, suggesting the use of a surrogate approach to screening for future evaluations.

titles.title: Nuclear Data Evaluation Utilizing Bayesian Monte Carlo Methods

abstracts.value: Cavity quantum magnonics has ushered in an unprecedented era of hybrid light-matter interfaces in which microwave photons, collective spin excitations, and superconducting or spin qubits can be coupled within a single device architecture, facilitating a versatile platform for quantum information processing. Realizing their full potential, however, requires a theory that can treat non-reciprocal magnetic media, material dissipation and open-cavity radiation losses, as well as finite-temperature fluctuations rigorously and without significant approximation. The dissipative magnonic resonances of such systems are described as quasinormal modes (QNMs), yet a consistent quantization procedure for lossy gyrotropic resonators has remained elusive. In this work, we present a finite-temperature quantum QNM theory, based on macroscopic quantum electrodynamics for non-reciprocal media and complex coordinate transformations, that achieves QNM quantization for a wide class of spatially inhomogeneous, dissipative and dispersive, cavity magnonic systems. We demonstrate the predictive capabilities of our theory via applications to hybrid dielectric-magnonic resonators interacting with both spin and superconducting qubits, evidencing modal interference effects, a continuous transition from coherent to dissipative coupling, spatiotemporal quantum field dynamics, and magnon-mediated qubit synchronization, at both zero and finite temperatures. By addressing the intricacies of modal loss and non-reciprocity in a fully quantum theory of cavity magnonics, our approach enables the quantitative design of hybrid quantum devices that operate under realistic open-system and thermal conditions, without recourse to ad hoc quantization schemes.

titles.title: Finite-temperature Quantum Quasinormal Mode Theory for Spatiotemporally-resolved Dissipative Cavity Quantum Magnonics

abstracts.value: We construct a density-dependent covariant energy density functional (CE-ME1) from full-Dirac-space relativistic Brueckner--Hartree--Fock (RBHF) self-energies and the corresponding equation of state. The space-like component $U_V$ is incorporated at the Fermi surface through reduced scalar and time-like self-energies, which are mapped onto local Hartree $σ$, $ω$, $δ$, and $ρ$ channels. The density-dependent couplings are represented by cubic Chebyshev polynomials over the density range $0.08\leqρ\leq0.48~{\rm fm}^{-3}$. A constrained thermodynamic calibration uses 199 RBHF energy-per-particle values from published microscopic computations at six isospin asymmetries, while maintaining positive, monotonic couplings. The Bonn-A RBHF saturation point, incompressibility $K_\infty=258$ MeV, symmetry energy $J=33.1$ MeV, and slope $L=65.2$ MeV are reproduced. The predicted curvature $K_{\rm sym}=33$ MeV differs from the published RBHF value of $-67$ MeV, illustrating the derivative sensitivity of the local reduction. The combined energy RMS is $0.613$ MeV, measuring model discrepancy rather than statistical uncertainty. Uniform matter remains mechanically stable and causal above saturation within the calibrated range. In cold charge-neutral $npeμ$ matter, CE-ME1 reasonably reproduces the interpolated RBHF pressure and proton fraction over most of the interval, although the pressure discrepancy increases near its upper edge. The DD-ME2 benchmark is stiffer and predicts a lower proton fraction at high density.

titles.title: Chebyshev-expanded covariant density functional from relativistic Brueckner theory

abstracts.value: We report the discovery of periodic radio bursts from the T8 brown dwarf WISE J151721.13+052929.3 (WISE J1517+05), detected with ASKAP and MeerKAT. The emission is characterised by a stable periodicity of $1.149 \pm 0.002$ hr, placing WISE J1517+05 among the fastest rotating radio-detected ultracool dwarfs (UCDs). The radio bursts are broadband and highly variable, reaching a peak spectral luminosity of $L_ν = 5.6 \times 10^{15}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$, making WISE J1517+05 the brightest periodic UCD to date. The high brightness temperature of the radio bursts ($T_B>10^{11}$ K), combined with the rotational modulation, strongly favour an auroral electron cyclotron maser emission (ECME) origin. In contrast to most known radio-bursting UCDs, the bursts exhibit relatively low and variable circular polarisation fractions (typically $\sim 20\%$). These properties suggest significant depolarisation of intrinsically highly polarised ECME, likely due to propagation effects in a structured magnetospheric plasma. Notably, we also observe a polarisation reversal within a single burst profile, which is currently unexplained. We model the emission using a dipolar magnetic field with emission arising from a single active field line, and find a moderate inclination angle of $i = 47.9^{+11.4}_{-9.2}$ degrees and a magnetic obliquity of $β= 40.1^{+9.2}_{-10.9}$ degrees. WISE J1517+05 expands the parameter space of radio-active UCDs toward higher luminosities and lower polarisation fractions, suggesting that current surveys may be sensitive to a larger population than previously recognised, while searches relying on methods that assume high circular polarisation fractions risk missing a subset of UCDs. More broadly, this discovery reinforces the idea that rapid rotation plays a key role in generating strong dipolar magnetic fields in UCDs that can give rise to auroral radio emission.

titles.title: Periodic radio emission from a rapidly rotating T8 ultracool dwarf

abstracts.value: Consensus algorithms are mechanisms driving nodes of a network to agreement. In quantum networks they also redistribute information encoded in the global quantum state, allowing global properties to be inferred from local measurements without reconstructing the global state. Motivated by this, we investigate decentralized quantum consensus in qudit networks governed by discrete random unitary dynamics. We characterize the analytic asymptotic dynamics, identify global information preserved by the evolution, and derive conditions for which different notions of quantum consensus emerge. A general theorem is derived that establishes a unified framework for extracting globally encoded information from local measurements beyond consensus states. First, we analyze CNOT networks and determine which global information can be recovered by individual nodes and which requires joint measurements on cooperating nodes. The CNOT model is well understood and presents a case with entanglement creation - a characteristic quantum feature of networks worth analyzing in detail. Second, we identify the complete class of two-qubit interactions that asymptotically achieve consensus on the average number of excitations, thereby establishing a quantum analogue of classical average consensus. We further show that joint measurements on k cooperating nodes recover exactly the first k moments of the excitation-number distribution.

titles.title: Consensus And Information Redistribution In Quantum Networks

abstracts.value: Spin-orbit coupling makes the mean position of a spinning particle transform anomalously under a Lorentz boost, with an additional shift known as a side jump. In this work, we develop a trace method to derive an exact but compact transformation kernel for the probability center of a general three-dimensional Dirac wave packet under an arbitrary finite Lorentz boost. The expression includes the physics of finite momentum width, spin-momentum correlations, and coherent phase structure without a semi-classical expansion. We identify texture-dependent side jumps even at fixed initial mean momentum, spin, and orbital angular momentum, as well as a non-monotonic mass dependence for Gaussian packets at fixed momentum width. The explicit kernels further resolve the spin and orbital angular-momentum contributions for massive and massless fermions, providing a kinematic basis for covariant particle-based spin transport that retains wave-packet information.

titles.title: Side jump and anomalous Lorentz transformation of a coherent Dirac wave packet

abstracts.value: In this study, we investigate the gravitational particle production (GPP) as a natural reheating channel in time-dependent backgrounds. We focus on reheating in an inflation-kination background. To maintain generality across inflationary models, we use a continuous scale-factor function that produces this transition and has been proposed in the literature. In this scenario, the gravitational reheating channel arises from the gravitational excitation of a superheavy spectator scalar field with Ricci-matter gravitational coupling. Besides all the perturbative approaches, a recently proposed non-perturbative one that uses the notion of the adiabatic vacuum has also been applied to the case of superheavy particles. Although the effect of the mass of the field on the reheating temperature has been investigated, the impact of the non-conformal values of the gravitational coupling constant on the GPP rate is not considered. Hence, we modify the non-perturbative approach in such a way that both effects can be traced. Three parameters affect the reheating temperature in this case: the bare mass of the field, the gravitational coupling constant, and the transition time. In this paper, the effect of each of these parameters alone on the resultant reheating temperature, as well as the combined effects of these parameters, is studied. Taking into account all involved parameters and surveying a wide range of the 3D parameter space, the highest reheating temperature possible is obtained. All of the aforementioned investigations are done based on numerical calculations, and we obtain that the highest possible reheating temperature is quite sufficient for the universe to enter the Hot Big-Bang era. For the sake of completeness, we study the GPP in such a transition using an analytical method in an independent, parallel, solvable model. This analysis is presented only as a mathematical tool.

titles.title: Non-Perturbative Approach to Gravitational Particle Production in the Inflation-Kination Transition: Surveying a Wide Range of the Parameter Space

abstracts.value: This work constructs an anisotropic, Einasto-profile fuzzy dark matter (DM) black hole (BH) using a logarithmically-corrected Starobinsky gravity, $f(R)=R+βR^2+γR^2\ln(R/μ^2)$, a form motivated by one-loop quantum corrections to the gravitational action rather than by the pure quadratic term alone. We derive the generalized trace equation for this action, show that its $β$- and $γ$-dependence collapses to a single compact source term, and solve the resulting field equations perturbatively about an exact general-relativistic (GR) background for two distinct anisotropic equations of state: a de~Sitter-type branch and a non-local branch, the latter worked through to a closed tangential-pressure profile rather than left incomplete. The logarithmic correction is found to raise the extremal (zero-temperature) threshold relative to pure quadratic gravity and to increase the core tangential pressure noticeably in the non-local branch.

titles.title: Structure of Logarithmically-Corrected Starobinsky Fuzzy Dark Matter Black Holes

Systematical decomposition of dimension-11
short-range neutrinoless double beta decay operators

Shi-Yu Lia∗ , Gui-Jun Dinga,b§

aDepartment of Modern Physics, and Anhui Center for fundamental sciences in theoretical physics,
University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, Anhui 230026, China

bCollege of Physics, Guizhou University, Guiyang 550025, China

Abstract

Neutrinoless double beta decay (0νββ) may receive sizable contributions from short-
range physics beyond the Standard Model. We present a systematical classification of all
tree-level ultraviolet completions of the dimension-11 short-range 0νββ decay operators,
renormalizable scenarios with scalar and fermion mediators are considered. We identify
eight distinct topologies and twenty-eight viable diagrams, from which all consistent
UV completions are generated by imposing Standard Model gauge invariance. All these
models involve a total of 61 new fields beyond the Standard Model and they typically
feature fractionally charged fermions and exotic bosons such as dileptons, diquarks,
and leptoquarks. We further study a representative model without colored mediators
and analyze its implications for the 0νββ decay half-life and light neutrino masses. We
find that current and future 0νββ decay experiments impose stringent constraints. Our
systematic decomposition provides a general framework for exploring exotic short-range
contributions to 0νββ decay in future experiments.

There are only left-handed neutrinos in the standard model (SM) so that neutrinos are
massless in SM. In order to generate tiny neutrino mass, one has to introduce new degree of
freedom which can be one or several new fermions or bosons. For instance, neutrinos could
be of Dirac particles as the other SM charged fermions by adding right-handed neutrinos
to the SM particle content, nevertheless this requires tiny Yukawa couplings of order 10−12.
The mass eigenstate of neutrino could be identical with that of antineutrino, i.e. neutrinos
are Majorana particle. Taking the particle content of the minimal SM, there is a unique
dimension-5 operator which is the famous Weinberg operator OW = 1

ΛNP

where L and H are the SM lepton doublets and Higgs fields respectively. After the electroweak
symmetry breaking, the Weinberg operator would lead to Majorana neutrino mass of order
v2/ΛNP. The non-renormalizable Weinberg operator can be mediated by the exchange of a
SM singlet fermion, a triplet scalar or a triplet fermion which correspond to the type I [6–9],
type II [10–15] and type III [16] seesaw mechanism respectively.

If neutrinos are Majorana fermions, the lepton number would be violated by two units by
the neutrino Majorana mass term. If neutrinos are Dirac particles, lepton number conserva-
tion is an exact law of nature and consequently the ∆L = 2 processes would be forbidden.
It is known that the search for neutrinoless double beta decay (0νββ decay) is are the most
sensitive probe of lepton number violation and Majorana neutrino mass. 0νββ decay is a
∆L = 2 rare nuclear decay process of the type (Z, A) → (Z + 2, A) + 2e− where the atomic
number Z increases by two units while the nucleon number A remains constant. Hence
this process takes place in a nucleus and converts two neutrons into two protons and two
electrons without outgoing antineutrinos. A positive signal of 0νββ decay would indicates
that neutrinos are Majorana particles [17]. Moreover, the observation of 0νββ can provide
important clues for understanding the neutrino mass generation mechanism and the origin
of the matter-antimatter asymmetry in our Universe. In addition, the 0νββ can also provide
insight to the flavor structure of SM, and it is a powerful tool to test and discriminate flavor
models. See Refs. [18–21] for recent review on 0νββ decay.

There are plenty of experiments searching for 0νββ decay with different isotopes. The
most stringent limit on the 136Xe decay half-life is T 0ν(136Xe) > 3.8×1026 yr from KamLAND-
Zen [22] at 90% confidence level, and the effective Majorana neutrino mass is constrained to
be in the region |mββ| ≡ |∑i U2

eimi| < (28 − 122) meV where the uncertainty on this bound
arises from the nuclear matrix element. The most sensitive limit on the 76Ge 0νββ decay half-
life is T1/2(76Ge) > 1.8×1026 yr from GERDA [23], which implies a bound |mββ| < (79−180)
meV. The next generation 0νββ experiments will increase the half-life sensitivity by a factor
of about 100, thus the effective Majorana neutrino mass |mββ| can be probed down to about
10 meV.

It is usually assumed that the 0νββ decay is dominantly induced by the exchange of
light Majorana neutrinos between two charged current interaction vertices, and thus the
decay amplitude is proportional to the effective mass mββ. Consequently it is usually called
mass mechanism. A priori one doesn’t know whether the mass mechanism dominates the
0νββ decay. The possible physics beyond the SM can also contribute to the 0νββ decay,
if it contains lepton number violating interactions. The energy transfer in 0νββ decay is
typically a few MeV. Thus at low energy below the electroweak scale, the SM gauge symmetry
SU(3)C × SU(2)L × U(1)Y is spontaneously broken down to SU(3)C × U(1)EM and the

range mechanism in the literature [24, 26]. Integrating out the heavy mediators, the 0νββ
decay can be described by non-renormalizable operators which are made of the SM fields
and invariant under the SM gauge group [24,25,29–31]. These operators involve at least four
quark fields and two lepton fields, consequently the lowest dimension is equal to nine. It turns
out that there are eleven electroweak invariant operators at dimension-9 and they lead to
eleven of the twenty-four operators in Eq. (1) at low energy [32]. The other thirteen operators
in Eq. (1) don’t occur at dimension-9 because they violate SM gauge invariance, twelve of
them are found to appear at dimension-11 and one of them at dimension-13. Systematical
analysis of the ultraviolet (UV) completions of the dimension-9 0νββ operators was presented
in Refs. [33, 34], it was found that there are two and six different topologies at tree [33] and
one-loop [34] level respectively.

In this work, we will focus on the 0νββ operators at dimension-11 that after electroweak
symmetry reduce to those operators in Eq. (1) which have not previously been found at
dimension-9. The aim is to identify all possible tree-level decompositions of these effective
operators and the corresponding new messenger fields would be listed out. We require that
the messengers can not mediate the short-range 0νββ operators of dimension-9, otherwise the
contributions of the concerned dimension-11 operators would be just some minor corrections
to the 0νββ decay. Due to the presence of the ∆L = 2 interactions in the decomposition
of the 0νββ operators, the light neutrinos are Majorana particles and the neutrino masses
mediated by the 0νββ messenger fields can be generated. The UV completions of these 0νββ
decay operators typically involve fractionally charged fermions and exotic bosons such as
dileptons, diquarks and leptoquarks, leading to rich collider and low-energy phenomenology.
Our analysis offers a general framework for probing exotic short-range contributions to 0νββ
decay in future experiments.

The rest of this paper is organized as follows. We shall present the short-range 0νββ
decay operators at dimension-11 in section 2. We provide all possible topologies, diagrams
and models together with the SM quantum numbers of the mediators in section 3. The
most minimal example model at dimension-11 is given in section 4, and the predictions for

4



the half-life of 0νββ decay and the light neutrino mass are studied. We summarize our
results and present our conclusions in section 5. The tree-level non-renormalizable topologies
for the dim-11 0νββ decay operators are collected in appendix A. The master formula for
the short-range 0νββ decay half-life, together with the corresponding low-energy effective

3 UV completions of the dim-11 0νββ decay operators
In the present work, we are interested in the tree-level renormalizable UV completions of

the dimension-11 0νββ decay operators, and we focus on the models in which the messengers
are scalar or fermion fields. The cases meditated by the SM gauge bosons or exotic vectors1

are neglected, although many of our results for scalar mediators also apply to diagrams with
vector mediators. The new fermion fields are assumed to be vector-like fermions under the SM
gauge symmetry in order to avoid the chiral anomaly. Following the diagrammatic approach
developed in [33, 36–41], we shall first find out the topologies of the tree-level Feynman
diagrams for the concerned 0νββ operators, then specify the Lorentz nature (spinor or scalar)
of each line, and finally fix the SM gauge quantum numbers of each messenger field by gauge
invariance.

operator should be absent, otherwise the tree-level contributions from the dim-11 0νββ op-

contribution is due to the absence of fields which generate 0νββ at lower order. That is to
say the messenger fields of the dim-11 0νββ operators are required to not mediate the lower
dim-9 0νββ operators. Notice that the lower order contribution could also be forbidden by
introducing additional discrete or gauge symmetries, however, the resulting models would be
much more complicated. It is well-known that the Majorana neutrino mass can be generated
by the interactions of 0νββ decay [17], the exchange of light Majorana neutrino can further
contribute to 0νββ decay. The Majorana neutrino masses can be effectively described by
the Weinberg operator. If the light Majorana neutrino masses are generated at tree level or
one-loop level, the mediators should be very heavy or their couplings with SM fields should
be very tiny in order to naturally accommodate the tiny neutrino masses. As a consequence,
the contribution of the dim-11 effective operators to 0νββ could be highly suppressed. Hence
we require that the tree level UV completion of the dim-11 0νββ operators should not con-
tain messengers which can mediate Weinberg operator through tree and one-loop Feynman
diagram. From Eq. (2), we see that the dim-11 0νββ operators involve either two Higgs fields
HH or their complex conjugate H∗H∗. If there is a 3-point vertex coupling two Higgs bosons
with a new scalar in the 0νββ decay diagrams of figure 2, the quantum number of the scalar
would be fixed to be (1,3, −1, S) or its complex conjugate which is exactly the mediator
of type-II seesaw mechanism. Therefore we have to exclude the diagrams which contain a
3-point vertex involving two external scalar lines. There are seven 0νββ diagrams in which
the two external Higgs fields are attached to a single 3-point vertex, as shown in figure 3.

5 Conclusion
The 0νββ decay, which violates lepton number by two units, is a sensitive probe of the

Majorana nature of neutrinos and offers valuable information on the neutrino mass spectrum
and mixing parameters. The standard interpretation assumes that 0νββ decay is dominated
by the exchange of light Majorana neutrinos. However, a wide class of scenarios beyond the
SM can also induce 0νββ decay. Such contributions are typically categorized into long-range
and short-range mechanisms, mediated by light neutrinos and heavy degrees of freedom,
respectively. At low energies, the effective Lagrangian describing 0νββ decay can be written
in terms of products of leptonic and hadronic currents. The ultraviolet completions of the
corresponding effective operators allow for a systematic exploration of the possible origins of
0νββ decay.

25



The effective Lagrangian for short-range 0νββ decay comprises twenty-four independent
operators with distinct Lorentz structures. Eleven of these operators originate from dim-9
operators which are invariant under the SM gauge symmetry. Among the remaining thirteen
operators, twelve arise from dim-11 SM invariant operators, while the last one first appears
at dimension thirteen. Both tree and one-loop decompositions of the dim-9 short-range
0νββ operators have been studied in Refs. [33, 34]. The present work provides a systematic
analysis of the tree-level decompositions of the dim-11 0νββ decay operators, identifying all
possible ultraviolet completions and the corresponding mediators. We restrict our analysis
to fermionic and scalar mediators, since introducing vector mediators beyond the SM gauge
bosons would necessitate an extension of the SM gauge symmetry. Nevertheless, many of our
results obtained for scalar mediators can be straightforwardly extended to scenarios involving
vector mediators.

The ultraviolet completions are assumed to be renormalizable above the electroweak
scale, consequently the allowed interaction vertices are restricted to scalar–scalar–scalar,
fermion–fermion–scalar, and scalar–scalar–scalar–scalar forms. The dim-11 0νββ operators
contain four quark fields, two lepton fields and two Higgs fields. We find eight distinct topolo-
gies for the tree-level decomposition of these operators, as shown in figure 1. By specifying
the Lorentz nature (scalar or fermion) of each line, the topologies can be promoted to dia-
grams. This yields twenty-eight possible diagrams with two external scalars and six external
fermion fields, shown in figure 4. Subsequently, the quark, lepton, and Higgs fields appearing
in the dim-11 0νββ operators are assigned to the external legs. The SM gauge quantum
numbers of all internal fields are then uniquely determined by requiring gauge invariance at
each interaction vertex. This procedure allows for a systematic generation of all possible UV
completions. Our analysis is restricted to models in which the leading contribution to 0νββ
decay arises from dim-11 operators. This condition excludes scenarios where the mediators
generate dim-9 short-range operators at tree level. Moreover, we impose that light Majorana
neutrino masses are induced no earlier than at two loops, so as to prevent the suppression of
the dim-11 contribution.

We identify a large class of models realizing the dim-11 0νββ decay operators, which are
collected in the supplementary file [42]. In total, these constructions involve 61 new fields
beyond the SM, which are summarized in table 3, with individual models involving three, four
or five mediators. They generically feature fractionally charged fermions and exotic bosons
such as dileptons, diquarks and leptoquarks. Consequently a rich collider phenomenology
is expected. Lepton number violating interactions are generically present and provide an
important probe of these models.

Nearly all ultraviolet completions involve colored mediator fields, with the exception of
two models presented in section 4 and appendix D, respectively. The first model requires
three colorless scalar fields: a diquark doublet ϕ, a dilepton singlet ζ, and a scalar doublet
η carrying exotic electric charges. The second model differs in that the dilepton scalar ζ is
replaced by an uncolored vector-like fermion doublet Ψ. For the first model, we investigate
the implications for the 0νββ decay half-life and the generation of light neutrino masses. We
find that forthcoming ton-scale 0νββ decay experiments place stringent constraints on the
allowed parameter space. The observed small neutrino masses can be achieved for mediator
masses in the range of few TeV, which is partially accessible at current and future colliders,

26



as well as in experiments searching for charged lepton flavour violation. The systematic
decomposition of dim-11 0νββ operators carried out in this work is expected to provide a
useful guide for identifying and interpreting exotic short-range contributions to 0νββ decay
if a signal is observed in forthcoming experiments.

A Non-renormalizable topologies of dim-11 0νββ decay
operators at tree-level

In addition to the eight topologies shown in figure 1, there are eleven further tree-level
topologies with eight external lines, displayed in figure 12. As can be seen, the dim-11 0νββ
decay operators in Eq. (2) contain six fermion fields and two scalar fields. When quark,
lepton, and Higgs fields are attached to the external lines, some interaction vertices necessarily
involve either two fermions and two scalars or four fermions, since Lorentz invariance requires
each interaction term in the Lagrangian to contain an even number of fermion fields. The
corresponding interaction terms therefore have mass dimension greater than four and are
non-renormalizable by power counting. In this work, we focus on renormalizable ultraviolet
(UV) completions of the dim-11 0νββ decay operators at tree level.

D.2 0νββ models with two new SU(3)C singlets and one new SU(3)C

triplet
We discuss the 0νββ decay models that involve colored fields in the following. We restrict

ourselves to the simple case in which only one color-triplet field beyond the SM is present.
Under this assumption, there exist only eight such models, which are summarized in table 4.
Each of these models contains two colorless fields and one color-triplet field. Apart from the
fields ζ, η, Ψ introduced in Eq. (3) and Eq. (49), the additional field multiplets are

χ ∼ (1,1, 1, S) , Γ ∼ (3,1, −1/3, F ) , Θ ∼ (3,1, 2/3, F ) ,

Ω ∼ (3,2, −5/6, F ) , ∆ ∼ (3,2, 7/6, F ) , (52)

where all fermionic fields transform as color triplets, while the scalar field is colorless. In
all these models, the light neutrino masses are generated at the two-loop level. The models
MF-3i-1, MF-3i-2, MF-3i-3, MF-3i-4, MF-3i-6, and MF-3i-7 contain two scalar fields and one
fermionic field, whereas the remaining models MF-3i-40 and MF-3i-41 involve one scalar field
and two fermionic fields. Remarkably, in the models MF-3i-1, MF-3i-2, MF-3i-3, and MF-3i-4
which are the UV completions of O2a,2b or O3a,3b, there exists only a single Feynman diagram
contributing to the 0νββ decay process. In all these four cases, the Feynman diagram is based
on the topology T4-6 and contains five propagators. Furthermore, all propagators appearing
in these diagrams correspond to new fields introduced in Eqs. (3, 49, 52).

The remaining four models, MF-3i-6, MF-3i-7, MF-3i-40 and MF-3i-41, provide UV com-
pletions of the effective operators O1a,1b, O2a,2b and O3a,3b. For each of these models, there
are twelve distinct Feynman diagrams contributing to the 0νββ decay process. All of these
diagrams involve five mediators, comprising three new fields as well as the SM Higgs field
and right-handed quarks. Following the same strategy as in section 4, the predictions for
the 0νββ decay half-life and the light neutrino masses can be obtained. However, the cor-
responding calculations are technically involved and lengthy, and are therefore deferred to
future work.

abstracts.value: We perform a comprehensive phenomenological analysis of neutrino masses, lepton-flavor violation, gravitational-wave signature induced by the first-order electroweak phase transition, and scalar dark matter within the framework of the singlet--triplet scotogenic model. We derive general analytical expressions for the one-loop Wilson coefficients of the penguin and box contributions to lepton-flavor-violating processes, considering generic scalar and fermion mediators. These general results are then applied to the singlet--triplet scotogenic model to calculate the branching ratios of $μ\to eγ$ and $μ\to e\overline{e}e$, as well as the coherent $μ$--$e$ conversion rate. We systematically investigate the lepton-flavor-violation phenomenology and the constraints from current and future experiments. It is found that the coupling $λ_5$ plays a key role in connecting neutrino masses, lepton flavor violation, and dark matter direct detection. We also study the finite-temperature effective potential and the gravitational-wave signatures of the resulting first-order phase transition. By analyzing the thermal history of the model, we identify the viable parameter space allowing for a first-order electroweak phase transition in the early Universe and find that the portal parameters $λ_1^Ω$ and $μ_1$ play a crucial role in determining the transition strength. The corresponding stochastic gravitational-wave spectra can be probed by future gravitational-wave observatories. As a representative example, we identify a benchmark point that simultaneously satisfies the current constraints from lepton-flavor-violation and dark-matter experiments and generates a stochastic gravitational-wave spectrum that may be probed by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, the Big Bang Observer, and the Ultimate Deci-hertz Interferometer Gravitational-wave Observatory.

abstracts.value: This work proposes a self-attention mechanism based on the fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine (FC-QBM), and further constructs a fully connected quantum Boltzmann machine language model (FC-QBM-LM) using the mechanism as the core engine. By performing unitary evolution on semantic quantum states, the mechanism implicitly implements positional encoding and self-attention computation, eliminating the need to decompose continuous semantic streams into discrete matrices for explicit matrix multiplication, with the measurement results naturally satisfying the normalization condition. Specifically, this work rigorously derives the computational principle of the self-attention mechanism based on FC-QBM, and demonstrates that this mechanism is mathematically equivalent to the classical self-attention mechanism. The mathematical principles governing the training and generation of FC-QBM-LM are thoroughly derived, and the two corresponding algorithms are subsequently developed. An 8-qubit FC-QBM-LM is finally constructed and trained on the corpus of Tang poetry. Under the 8-qubit setting, the quantum layer implements the entire positional encoding and self-attention computation pipeline with only 44 parameters. In the noiseless scenario, the model exhibits favorable convergence. Furthermore, the quantum circuit proposed in this work, which terminates with Y-axis rotation gates, achieves better convergence than the counterpart terminating with X-axis rotation gates. Under the small-sample regime and across eight distinct noise intensity levels, the model demonstrates strong noise robustness, retaining over 99% of its noiseless convergence performance. Experiments on five-character quatrain generation reveal that the model preliminarily exhibits three core capabilities: associative and divergent thinking, content generation across imagery and human-aligned word ordering.

titles.title: Wave Is All You Need: A Quantum Language Model Based on Fully Connected Quantum Boltzmann Machine

abstracts.value: We investigate the signatures of phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator and propose an optomechanical protocol to experimentally characterize it through Stokes-like measurements of an optical field. Starting from a deformed phase-space algebra characterized by the position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters $θ$ and $η$, we employ the Darboux transformation to construct an equivalent Hamiltonian in canonical variables. The resulting effective dynamics exhibits correlations between the oscillator degrees of freedom. We derive the corresponding covariance matrix and examine how the noncommutative parameters enter the mechanical dynamics and the optical response. By coupling the oscillator to a coherent optical probe, we obtain analytical expressions for the time-dependent optical coherence attenuation and the nonlinear Kerr phase. We then formulate an interferometric detection scheme through Stokes-like measurements, in which the outgoing optical field is combined with a phase-controlled reference beam at a balanced beam splitter, and the resulting photocurrents are measured using photodetectors. The optical response provides access to the modified normal-mode frequencies, which enables us to estimate experimental values of $θ$ and $η$. Our results establish a theoretical connection between NC-space dynamics, Gaussian-state correlations, and experimentally accessible optical observables, suggesting an optomechanical route toward testing signatures of phase-space noncommutativity.

titles.title: Estimation of covariance matrix for Stokes-like measurement under phase-space deformation

abstracts.value: We establish global control of perturbative D-term data governing semiclassical vacuum sectors in chiral supersymmetric gauge theories on $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$. A closed-form, one-loop-exact D-term coefficient, including 4d Fayet--Iliopoulos (FI) parameters, gives a uniformly controlled leading potential away from massless thresholds and fixes local FI and Chern--Simons couplings near them. This allows lifting the 3d Intriligator--Seiberg classification of semiclassical vacua to $\mathbb{R}^3\times S^1$ across the compact holonomy space. The framework is showcased by finding a remarkably rich set of vacuum sectors in a simple abelian model and reproducing on flat space the R-twisted reduction of an $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Maruyoshi--Song theory to the Gang--Yamazaki theory, first found on $S^3\times S^1$. The examples demonstrate the stakes of global matching: true vacua may lie at nontrivial holonomy even with nonzero threshold values of the Coulomb-slice D-coefficient, and despite vanishing D-coefficient at trivial holonomy.

titles.title: Perturbative Holonomy Potentials and Vacua in Chiral Supersymmetric Gauge Theories

abstracts.value: Collins, Hayden, and Nechita used free probability to construct families of $k$-positive but not $(k+1)$-positive maps and applied them to entanglement detection. We prove that positive free maps associated with compactly supported freely infinitely divisible distributions are no stronger than the reduction criterion in every ancillary dimension. In particular, these maps cannot detect positive partial transpose entanglement. The proof combines a joint Fock realization with an operator positivity certificate derived from free Lévy data.

titles.title: A Reduction Bound for Entanglement Detection by Positive Free Maps

abstracts.value: Using the analytic machinery and numerical inputs of OpenAI's proofs of the Haldane gap, we prove uniqueness of the translation-invariant ground state of the infinite $S=1$ Heisenberg antiferromagnetic chain and of the $J$-$D$ model for sufficiently small $|D|$. Uniqueness is among all translation-invariant ground states in the operator-algebraic sense, without assuming a gap or spin-rotation symmetry for a competing state. The proof combines concentration of the spatial transfer spectrum, an exponentially small low-temperature free-energy correction, and a Golden--Thompson comparison for separated local observables. The unique translation-invariant state is pure, locally unique and gapped, and continuous in $D$. The ground states of even periodic chains and odd open chains with equal positive endpoint fields converge to this state along their full sequences, uniformly in $D$, with a stretched-exponential local rate. Every choice of ground states of open chains without endpoint magnetic fields has the same local limit. These conclusions do not establish uniqueness among arbitrary nontranslation-invariant ground states of the infinite chain. The author formulated the problems and proposed the core strategies. ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to developing the proofs and preparing the manuscript.

abstracts.value: Path integral control is a stochastic optimal control framework that computes optimal policies as weighted averages over state trajectories. It was recently shown that, combined with stochastic quantum trajectories, the path integral control approach constitutes a promising alternative for quantum optimal control. In this work, we propose an extension of path integral control to the complex plane using circular complex Wiener processes. The change of measure is defined on the driving noise space under an exact control-noise matching condition, which also accommodates rank-deficient state diffusions. Applied to stochastic Schrödinger equations, the resulting formalism gives a compact treatment of paired non-Hermitian jump channels with unequal positive dissipation rates and yields cross-entropy-optimal feedback and open-loop control formulas.

titles.title: Path integral control in the complex plane

abstracts.value: We establish a new iterative method for computing rigorous lower bounds for the ground-state energies of all atoms and ions. The accuracy of the resulting bounds depends on two ingredients: the quality of the initial energy estimate and the quality of the used upper bound for the maximum number of bound electrons, $N_c(Z)$, as a function of the nuclear charge $Z>0$. In particular, this new method allows us to establish the explicit lower bound $E(N,Z) \geq -0.8710\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for the ground-state energy $E(N,Z)$ of the atom/ion with $N \in \mathbb{N}$ electrons and nuclear charge $Z \in (0,N]$, thereby considerably improving the best known constant $A=(3/2)^{1/3} \approx 1.1447$ in the estimate $E(N,Z) \geq -A\,N^{1/3}Z^2$ for $0 < Z \leq N$ and coming much closer to the best possible constant given by the Thomas-Fermi asymptotics $\lim_{N \to \infty} |E(N,N)|N^{-7/3}= -E_{\text{TF}}(1)\approx 0.7687$ derived in Adv. Math., 23(1) by Lieb and Simon. To demonstrate the potential and the limits of our method, we also compute explicit lower bounds for the ground-state energies $E(N,N)$ of all atoms with $2 \leq N \leq 86$ and we compare them with the bounds obtained in J. Chem. Phys., 62(8) by Hertel, Lieb, Thirring and the bounds obtained by Seco in his dissertation. Finally, we also provide a uniqueness result for the expectation values of the kinetic, potential and interaction energies on the ground-state space.

titles.title: Rigorous Lower Bounds for Atomic and Ionic Ground-State Energies

abstracts.value: We construct smooth Riemannian metrics and scalar potentials that are invariant under a circle action and satisfy the static Einstein equations with positive cosmological constant. The underlying compact three-manifold is a ball with two disjoint open balls removed. The potential (or lapse function) is positive in the interior and vanishes at the boundary, consisting of three non-degenerate horizons. The areas of the two inner boundary components are controlled by two arbitrary parameters, namely the masses of the black holes, which are taken to be sufficiently small and comparable. Each inner horizon radius scales linearly with the individual mass parameters, while the separation of their reference centers scales as the cube root of the total mass. These two scales are assumed to be sufficiently small at different rates, whereas the cosmological length remains fixed. The main analytical challenge is to control the linearized equation and the nonlinear remainder simultaneously near the shrinking horizons, between the centers and in the outer region. Weighted Hölder estimates quantify the growth of the inverse and show that the error of an approximation joining Kottler collars to de Sitter space is small enough to close a contraction argument. Namely, we solve a reduced elliptic Einstein equation that is endowed with two obstruction tensors; varying the two axial positions removes their coefficients. The contracted Bianchi identity and an energy estimate for an auxiliary vector field (Killing field) introduced by the projection to vanish. Finally, for a fixed cosmological constant, the intrinsic metric of one of the two boundary components is sufficient to determine a static solution with simply connected interior and non-vanishing boundary gradient, up to isometry and multiplication of the potential by a positive constant.

titles.title: Existence of static axisymmetric solutions to the Einstein equations

abstracts.value: We consider the Pauli-Fierz model of one spinless non-relativistic electron coupled to the quantized transverse electromagnetic field, without external potential, with a sharp ultraviolet cutoff Lambda and bare mass m. Let h = m_eff/m be the ratio of the effective mass, defined by the curvature of the fiber ground state energy at total momentum zero, to the bare mass; by scaling, h depends only on the fine structure constant alpha = e^2/(4 pi) and on lambda = Lambda/m. We prove two lower bounds. First, h >= 1 + 0.3441 alpha/(1 + 0.2985 sqrt(alpha) + 0.1252 alpha) for all alpha > 0 and all lambda >= 1; the bound does not depend on the cutoff, and with the band extended to the cutoff its first order coefficient in alpha is the perturbative one of Hiroshima and Spohn. The proof uses a coherent translation of the field applied to the ground state as a trial state; the term linear in the translation vanishes by minimality of the ground state. Second, for every fixed alpha, h grows faster than linearly: for every epsilon > 0, h >= lambda^(8/7 - epsilon) for all large lambda (8/7 is the limit of the method). Consequently iota_PF(alpha) := inf_{lambda > 0} h/lambda > 0, and for a fixed physical mass m_phys a bare mass reproducing it exists only if Lambda <= m_phys/iota_PF(alpha). This was expected, but not proved, by Lieb and Loss (2002). The proof of the second bound starts from the sharp self-energy asymptotics of a companion paper and uses a trial state obtained from the ground state by a phase depending on the field configuration. The new ingredients are an estimator for the position of the electron given by the local centre of a shallow level set of the photon cloud, the decoupling of a localized part of the field from the electron through a divergence-free external subspace, and a proof that shallow depressions near the edge of the localization window are rare.

titles.title: The effective mass of the Pauli-Fierz electron: a cutoff-independent lower bound and the breakdown of mass renormalization

abstracts.value: Let $f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ with an isolated critical point at the origin. The Calabi--Yau/Landau--Ginzburg correspondence predicts a close relation between invariants of the Landau--Ginzburg orbifold $(\mathbb C^n/\mathbb Z_n,f)$ and those of the associated Calabi--Yau hypersurface $ X_f=\{[z_1:\cdots:z_n]\in\mathbb P^{n-1}:f(z_1,\ldots,z_n)=0\}. $ In this paper, we establish this correspondence for the genus-one B-model by constructing the Landau--Ginzburg genus-one B-model invariant intrinsically from the $f$-twisted Laplacian on $\mathbb{C}^n/\mathbb{Z}_n$ and proving that it agrees with the corresponding BCOV invariant of $X_f$ up to an additive constant depending only on the dimension.

abstracts.value: Monodromy defects are fundamental objects in extended quantum systems with global symmetries. We study such defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories (CFT), which describe the universality class of $\text{O}(N)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking transitions. In particular, we consider partial-monodromy defects, whose corresponding symmetry transformations only act on a subset of the fundamental $\text{O}(N)$ vector field. We develop an analytical theory of the defect phases, using both renormalization group and large $N$ expansion. In general (spacetime) dimensions $3\leq d<4$, multiple defect CFTs are identified, which are described by appropriate boundary conditions for the vector field near the defect. Near $d=3$, we show that in the large $N$ limit, a stable defect CFT always exists, characterized by the so-called ("standard") "alternate" boundary conditions for the (twisted) untwisted fields, whose defect correlations are (suppressed) enhanced. We then perform large-scale classical Monte Carlo simulations of monodromy defects in the O(3) CFT in an improved lattice model and numerically extract the defect scaling dimensions. The numerical results are in qualitative agreement with the stable defect CFT identified in the field theory.

titles.title: Revisiting monodromy defects in $\text{O}(N)$ conformal field theories

abstracts.value: Quantum processing units (QPUs) require frequent benchmarking to track hardware drift, yet standard protocols such as randomized benchmarking are resource-intensive and compete with application workloads for scarce QPU time. We present a resource-optimal screening strategy that combines a two-tier, risk-based testing architecture with optimal experiment design: a lightweight screening probe runs regularly and triggers expensive full characterization only when statistically significant change is detected, while the probe itself is designed to maximize detection sensitivity under explicit resource constraints. For an exponential fidelity model, we derive closed-form optimal circuit sizes and introduce an effective gate count that renders the analysis hardware-independent. We instantiate the strategy for two applications. For gate-quality verification, we show that optimally designed screening probes outperform randomized benchmarking with optimal experimental design (OED) by more than 4$\times$ in detection rate at equal resource cost. For compiler benchmarking, we formalize compiler comparison as a paired hypothesis test and derive the optimal circuit size for distinguishing compilation strategies. Despite their different observables and test statistics, both applications yield structurally the same closed-form expression for the optimal probe circuit size as a function of gate fidelity, illustrating the generality of the framework. Numerical and hardware experiments on QPUs (Rigetti Ankaa-3, IQM Garnet, IQM Emerald) confirm the theoretical predictions, with observed optimal circuit sizes matching the derived values across all devices.

titles.title: Resource-Optimal Screening for Two-Tier Quantum System Characterization

abstracts.value: This Comment clarifies the physical interpretation of the black hole spacetime metric employed by Shaymatov \textit{et al.} [Phys. Dark Univ. 34 (2021) 100891]. We point out that the metric, originally derived in Li and Yang (2012), describes a specific dual-component system consisting of cold dark matter and a phantom field background. Treating this geometry as a single-component ``Perfect Fluid Dark Matter'' (PFDM) with a total equation of state $w_{\mathrm{total}} = -1$ is physically incompatible with the gravitational attraction required for dark matter halos. Furthermore, we clarify the distinct parameter regimes of the original model to prevent potential misapplications in extreme astrophysical scenarios.

abstracts.value: We present laboratory experiments on the early stage of the formation process of quasi-perpendicular supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks using laser-produced plasmas in an ambient uniform nitrogen (N) gas with 1~Torr under the external magnetic field with controlled polarity. An expanding aluminum (Al) piston plasma arising from laser irradiation interacts with a magnetized ambient N plasma, producing a bright, asymmetric self-emission whose global morphology reverses with the magnetic-field polarity. Two-dimensional ideal-magnetohydrodynamics simulations reproduce the main features of the observed structures and indicate that the ripple formation is unlikely to be driven by the Kelvin--Helmholtz instability, but is instead associated with vortex formation at the rounded leading edge of the piston plasma. We show that the bright, rippling emission delineates the Al-N interface, whose intrinsic width is consistent with an electron kinetic scale, and that its upstream side is predominantly composed of N plasma. This identification allows the formation of a supercritical collisionless shock in the magnetized N plasma to be discussed with minimal Al contamination.

titles.title: Identification of rippling interface between laser-ablated plasma and ambient uniform plasma at rest

abstracts.value:
We present a complete dispersive evaluation of the Bernabéu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach (BEFT) sum rule for the nucleon dipole polarizability difference $α_{E1}-β_{M1}$. The analysis is based on hyperbolic dispersion relations, which separate the $s$- and $t$-channel contributions without double counting and are particularly suited to backward real Compton scattering. This framework makes it possible to precisely determine the polarizability difference from independent dispersive input rather than from fits to low-energy Compton scattering data. The $s$-channel part is updated with modern single-pion photoproduction multipoles and model estimates of non-$πN$ inelastic channels. For the $t$-channel, we use contemporary dispersive input for $γγ\toππ/K\bar K_{I_t=0}$ together with Roy-Steiner equation solutions for $ππ/K\bar K_{I_t=0}\to N\bar N$, and we extend the calculation to the isovector $πη/K\bar K_{I_t=1}$ channel associated with the $a_0(980)$. The resulting treatment resolves the long-standing puzzle of earlier BEFT evaluations driven by the scalar-isoscalar two-pion channel and gives a controlled estimate of the subleading isovector contribution. Combining the resulting BEFT values with the Baldin sum rule, we obtain, in units of $10^{-4}\,\mathrm{fm}^3$, 
\[ α_{E1}^p=11.17(52),\quad β_{M1}^p=2.84(52),\quad α_{E1}^n=12.18(59),\quad β_{M1}^n=3.03(59). \]
 For the proton, these values provide a benchmark with a precision comparable to state-of-the-art dispersive and chiral effective field theory extractions. For the neutron, whose polarizabilities are much less directly constrained experimentally, the result provides an independent dispersive benchmark with an uncertainty comparable to that of the proton.

titles.title: Nucleon polarizabilities revisited: insights from the Bernabéu-Ericson-Ferro Fontan-Tarrach sum rule

abstracts.value: Quantum machine learning uses quantum states and dynamics to represent and process data. In quantum reservoir computing, the physical system is typically fixed and a classical readout is trained. Inspired by the formation, strengthening and pruning of synapses during biological learning, we propose quantum neuroplastic learning (QNL), which reorganizes the couplings among the qubits of a quantum reservoir, much as experience rewires connections among neurons. Eligibility traces guide local edits to couplings, fields, gate angles and evolution time, and an edit is retained when a statistical bound on its improvement exceeds a complexity cost. We evaluate QNL under restarting and online monitored protocols on short- and long-term memory, nonlinear autoregressive processing and forecasting, and channel equalization tasks. In simulation, QNL enhances memory capacity, develops long-term recall and sustains adaptation across multiple tasks, with the largest benefit for tasks that require extended memory. On the IBM superconducting processor \texttt{ibm\_fez}, with six seven-qubit reservoirs running in parallel on 42 qubits (1.28 million shots in total), configurations learned in simulation and frozen before execution reduced the channel-equalization symbol error rate from 9.7% to 2.2% and achieved a lower error rate than a matched-budget tuned baseline.

titles.title: Quantum neuroplastic learning for time-series processing

abstracts.value: The nonlinear iterative repetitive Penrose process established recently by Ruffini et al. is generalized to the magnetic Penrose process. The spacetime background is the Kerr metric, the external magnetic field is described by the Wald solution, the electromagnetic field is treated as a test field, and the charge is treated as a test charge. We analyze the optimal conditions for maximum energy extraction on the equatorial plane and find that under these conditions the core mechanism of the iterative process is charging feedback. After charging, the black hole charge is approximately half of the Wald charge. When the neutral parent particle decays, charge conservation forces the infalling fragment to carry charge while the other fragment carries the opposite charge, so the black hole charge accumulates monotonically. The monopole voltage of the Wald solution decreases linearly with the charge $Q$ and crosses zero to reverse sign at a certain point, so the magnetic gain is gradually neutralized by the charge. The repetitive magnetic Penrose process is therefore forced to terminate and eventually falls back to the mechanical Penrose process. The energy extraction efficiency $>100\%$ predicted by the single magnetic Penrose process will therefore be prevented.

titles.title: Repetitive Magnetic Penrose Process

abstracts.value: The properties of hadrons in dense matter have been a core interest of mine since I entered graduate school at Stony Brook in 1984. This interest was shaped both by the strong research activity on the subject at Stony Brook at the time and by the influence of Mannque Rho, who was a frequent visitor there. In this memoir dedicated to Mannque, I describe a selection of his works that sparked my interest in the subject and present my current perspective on what Mannque, together with Gerry Brown, sought to emphasize in the often-misinterpreted Brown--Rho scaling. In light of recent developments, I also discuss refinements of Brown--Rho scaling for mesons and baryons, associated with spontaneous chiral symmetry breaking and $U_A(1)$-breaking effects.

titles.title: Remembering Brown-Rho scaling

abstracts.value: We describe the final quasar sample from the Southern part of the All-sky BRIght, Complete Quasar Survey (AllBRICQS), which aimed to discover the remaining optically bright quasars using data from Gaia and WISE. We discuss our final selection and present a further 119 quasars in the redshift range $z=[0.03;4.35]$. This brings the sample of spectroscopically confirmed quasars with $G_{\rm RP}<16$ and $z>0.1$ at Dec$<+20^{\circ}$ and Galactic latitude $|b|>10^{\circ}$ to 745 objects. The spectra from the ANU 2.3m telescope at Siding Spring Observatory cover a wavelength range from 360 to 950 nm with $R\sim3000$. For redshifts of $z>0.12$, we expect the sample to be complete at $G_{\rm RP}<16$, a regime that is usually avoided by large spectroscopic surveys due to detector saturation. We note that at least one strongly lensed quasar has escaped our selection.

titles.title: AllBRICQS: the All-sky BRIght, Complete Quasar Survey - Quasar Selection and Final Southern $G_{\rm RP}<16$ Sample

abstracts.value: Supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks require ion reflection for dissipation, yet its role during formation remains unclear. Using high-power lasers, self-emission imaging, and collective Thomson scattering, we investigate a forming quasi-perpendicular shock. An upstream emission tail is consistent with a foot-like structure, while ion heating and temperature anisotropy extend upstream of a ramp-like region. These observations provide evidence of reflected-ion-related heating during early shock formation, although the incident and reflected ion populations are not separately resolved. Future measurements of ion distributions and plasma waves could clarify how this heating mediates shock dissipation and particle energization.

titles.title: Experimental Evidence for Reflected Ions and Ion Temperature Anisotropy in a Forming Supercritical Magnetized Collisionless Shock

abstracts.value: We consider a nonrelativistic gravity theory in (2+1) dimensions with $w_\infty$ gauge symmetry that we call unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity. The theory has three dimensionless couplings, one of which is the Chern-Simons level $κ$. At large $|κ|$, the theory flows from an asymptotically free UV fixed point to an IR fixed point with anisotropic scale invariance characterized by a dynamical critical exponent $z=2-\tfrac32|κ|^{-1}$. We speculate that unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons gravity undergoes a phase transition from this scale-invariant phase to a confining phase when $κ$ drops below a critical value.

titles.title: Lifshitz Phase of Quantum Gravity: The Infrared Fixed Point of the (2+1)D Unimodular Hořava-Chern-Simons Model

abstracts.value: We give a direct analytic proof that every total Boolean function computable exactly with at most two quantum queries depends on at most six input variables. This bound is sharp. A previous derivation relied on a numerical classification of Boolean functions on at most four variables; to the best of our knowledge, ours is the first unconditional proof. The main difficulty beyond the one-query case is that query-path vectors need not be mutually orthogonal, so interference prevents the scalar weight-counting argument from applying. We overcome this difficulty by establishing a rigid support-and-branch decomposition: after the coordinates in the first-query support are fixed, the second query induces a family of exact one-query branches. This structural description may be of independent interest.

titles.title: Two exact quantum queries use at most six variables

abstracts.value: The geometric structure of atomic nuclei plays an important role in shaping the initial conditions of high-energy nuclear collisions and the subsequent evolution of the quark--gluon plasma. In this work, we develop a multimodal deep-learning framework to infer the Woods--Saxon radius ($R_0$) and diffuseness parameter ($a$) from initial-state information. Using the TRENTo model for relativistic $^{238}$U+$^{238}$U collisions, we construct a dataset covering multiple combinations of $R_0$ and $a$, and perform parameter regression by combining two-dimensional entropy-density distributions with event-level scalar observables, including multiplicity and eccentricities $\varepsilon_2$--$\varepsilon_5$. The results show that the proposed framework can effectively recover the Woods--Saxon parameters from initial-state information. Joint multi-event inputs suppress statistical fluctuations and improve regression performance by enhancing the extraction of collective information. The inversion accuracy exhibits a pronounced centrality dependence: $R_0$ is best constrained in central collisions, whereas $a$ shows the strongest sensitivity in the mid-peripheral region and becomes less well constrained in ultra-central and peripheral collisions. These findings indicate that the initial-state geometry retains useful information about nuclear radial structure and provide a baseline for future studies that incorporate transport evolution and experimental final-state observables.

titles.title: Inferring Nuclear Radial Parameters from Initial-State Information in Heavy-Ion Collisions Using Deep Neural Networks

abstracts.value: EP241021a is a peculiar fast X-ray transient exhibiting a long X-ray plateau and an optical rebrightening, both challenging the traditional jet afterglow model. Whether its nature is a stellar explosion or a tidal disruption event (TDE) remains debated. Here we present late-time HST/WFC3 and Gemini-N/GMOS observations of its host galaxy at $z=0.748$. After $\sim300$ days post-trigger, the transient emission had faded below detection, revealing a dwarf disk galaxy with an effective radius $R_e=1.7$ kpc, a stellar mass $M_\star\sim3\times10^8M_\odot$, and a high star formation rate of $\sim5\ M_\odot\ {\rm yr}^{-1}$. Combined with previous very long baseline interferometry measurements, the transient can be located in the galactic disk with a projected physical offset of $0.95\pm0.13$ kpc from the galaxy center. Host-subtracted optical light curves show that the rebrightening ceased at $\sim47$ days, followed by a sudden drop with a power-law index steeper than $-3.3$, coincident with a similar drop in the X-ray light curve. This synchronous drop in both bands is consistent with jet shut-off, and the required month-long jet activity suggests a persistently accreting compact object fed by a TDE. Among the TDE scenarios, the off-nuclear location and the starburst host galaxy slightly favor the post-supernova micro-TDE scenario in a binary system, in which a natal kick drives the newborn compact object into a tidal disruption of its companion. Nevertheless, an off-nuclear intermediate-mass black hole TDE or a stellar-mass black hole TDE induced by dynamical scattering in a dense stellar cluster cannot yet be excluded.

titles.title: EP241021a as An Off-nuclear Month-duration Transient in a Dwarf Starburst Galaxy

abstracts.value: We use the ELUCID simulation to study how the local environment affects the formation of dark matter halos and their spatial distribution around the cosmic web. We describe the environment by local density and cosmic-web type. At fixed web type, the halo mass function (HMF) depends strongly on the local density, whereas at fixed density it depends only weakly, though significantly, on the web type; the character of both dependencies changes around the mean density. The halo formation redshift is primarily driven by local density rather than cosmic web. We then introduce the three-dimensional cosmic-web cross-correlation function (3D-WCCF), which expresses the distribution of halos around cosmic web in the local tidal eigenframe. The 3D-WCCF provides numerous anisotropic characteristics. Around all web types, halos are most strongly correlated along the axis of weakest compression, $\mathbf{e}_3$, and least along the axis of strongest compression, $\mathbf{e}_1$. Nearly all cluster-sized halos reside in knots and lie preferentially in the plane perpendicular to ${\bf e}_1$. The 3D-WCCF also provides important information on the geometry and size of filaments, sheets and voids. Moreover, early-forming halos are more strongly correlated with the web than late-forming ones, and this assembly bias is anisotropic around filaments, sheets, and voids, being strongest along $\mathbf{e}_3$, but nearly isotropic around knots.

titles.title: Halo formation and distribution around cosmic web

abstracts.value: We calculate the decay rate for the radiative Higgs decay $H \to ψ(4230) + γ$ within and beyond the SM. The vector state $ψ(4230)$ is a candidate exotic tetraquark state and has the quantum numbers $I^G(J^{PC})=0^-(1^{--})$, having a mass $m_{ψ(4230)}=4221.7 \pm 2.5$ MeV and a decay width $Γ_{ψ(4230)}=51 \pm 7$ MeV. We propose a practical parametrization of the so-called {\it direct amplitude}, using the leptonic coupling of the $ψ(4230)$ to estimate the short-distance overlap relevant to the Higgs decay amplitude. We find ${\cal B}_{\rm SM}( H \to ψ(4230) γ)=4.88^{+4.71}_{-4.52}\times 10^{-7}$, where the uncertainties are dominated by the experimental uncertainty in the leptonic decay width of the $ψ(4230)$. The branching ratio increases to about $10^{-6}$ for $y_c=-3 $, where $y_c$ is the Higgs-Yukawa coupling of the charm quark.

titles.title: Radiative Higgs decay to $ψ\left(4230\right)$

abstracts.value: Quantum measurement can profoundly impact the dynamics of many-body systems, for instance, inducing phase transitions from volume-law chaotic phases to area-law localized phases. While chaotic phases emerge naturally in generic many-body systems, the experimental realization of a fully localized phase driven by measurement remains challenging, primarily owing to the stringent requirement of near-perfect isolation of the system from environmental dissipation. Here we experimentally observe measurement-induced localization phenomena in an interacting $^{13}\mathrm{C}$ nuclear spin system in diamond. In contrast to previous circuit-model-based experiments, our well-isolated system evolves under a physical many-body Hamiltonian with measurements intervening at intervals. By implementing either projective measurements on a single spin or global weak measurements on the entire system, we observe substantially prolonged spin autocorrelation times as the measurement frequency increases. Our results, combined with numerical simulations, provide evidence that quantum measurement can drive a many-body system into a localized regime, and lay the groundwork for future experimental investigations into measurement-induced many-body dynamics and related entanglement phenomena.

titles.title: Observation of measurement-induced localization phenomena in a solid-state spin system

abstracts.value: Practical fault-tolerant quantum computation requires a large number of physical qubits, posing a major challenge for scaling up individual quantum processors. Distributed architectures offer a promising solution by interconnecting multiple processors through quantum networks. However, remote Bell-pair generation remains technically demanding, making it essential to assess computational performance under limited communication resources. In this work, we present a comprehensive resource analysis of distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation using superconducting processors connected by microwave or optical links. We show that even a single physical communication channel per node can substantially reduce the physical-qubit requirements per node under experimentally motivated, forward-looking microwave-link assumptions of a 1 MHz physical Bell-pair generation rate and 90% fidelity, although at the cost of a roughly tenfold increase in execution time. Conversely, reducing the execution-time overhead requires substantially greater communication resources, including higher Bell-pair fidelities and extensive multiplexing. These results demonstrate the potential feasibility of distributed fault-tolerant quantum computation with limited communication resources and provide a quantitative basis for balancing quantum-link performance, processor size, and execution time.

titles.title: Feasibility of Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing: From Quantum Links to Algorithms

abstracts.value: We show that a vibration shared by two emitter subensembles can jointly establish multiphoton resonance and constructive interference among the virtual exchange pathways responsible for coherent conversion. For opposite displacements with an integer magnitude ratio $r\geq2$, the displacements induced by $r$ excitations in the less displaced subensemble and one in the other cancel exactly, a condition we call displacement neutrality. When the emitter and cavity frequencies match, the resulting composite is resonant with $r+1$ cavity photons, while the vibration-mediated cross interaction makes the conversion pathways add constructively, establishing a direct relation between the displacement ratio and the conversion order. In contrast, independent vibrations can be tuned to the same resonance, but their conversion pathways cancel at leading order, demonstrating that energy resonance alone does not guarantee coherent conversion. For $r=2$, this conversion suppresses three-photon coincidences while leaving the two-photon statistics nearly Poissonian. In the weak-driving limit, interference can also screen the two-photon correlations at all delays from the relative direction of the displacements, whereas the three-photon statistics remain sensitive to it. Because both resonant states leave the vibration undisplaced, their coherence is protected from direct dephasing by the shared vibration, leaving emitter dephasing as the tighter constraint. These results identify relative vibrational displacements as a means of controlling coherent multiphoton conversion and its noise response.

titles.title: Resonant Multiphoton Conversion Mediated by a Shared Vibration in Cavity QED
